Rent Increase Limits
Maximum rent increase:
Your landlord can only raise your rent by a certain amount each year. The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

content.text: Landlords can only raise rent by a certain amount each year, with the increase capped at no more than 3% of current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

citations.cited_text: If a landlord charges a tenant a pass-through fee greater than $50, the landlord shall reimburse the tenant for the registration fee pass-through overpayment.

content.text: If a landlord charges a tenant a pass-through fee greater than $50, the landlord shall reimburse the tenant for the registration fee pass-through overpayment.

citations.cited_text:
The pass-through fee is charged by rental unit, not by the number of tenants in a rental unit. For example:
If Unit A has 5 tenants, the pass-through fee is $50.
If Unit B has 1 tenant, the pass-through fee is $50.

content.text: The pass-through fee is charged by rental unit, not by the number of tenants in a rental unit.

citations.cited_text:
Renter Protections
Just cause evictions:
Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

content.text: Landlords must have a valid reason to evict tenants, which could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

citations.cited_text:
Relocation assistance:
If your landlord evicts you for certain reasons, they might have to help pay for your moving costs.

content.text: If landlords evict tenants for certain reasons, they might have to help pay for moving costs.
